rules.rationale: High halogen counts add hydrophobic surface and polarizable volume, the dominant driver of octanol-water partitioning.
Extended aromatic frameworks are poorly hydrated and raise logD independent of chain length.
Halogenated aromatics combine pi-density with lipophilic surface, a mechanistically additive partition gain.
Stronger reweighting of heteroatom polarity, since the prior generation underweighted the dominant aqueous-partitioning penalty.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the winning halogen/aromatic partition signal but rebalances weight toward heteroatom polarity, which the feedback suggests was under-penalized rather than over-penalized. Fails if size effects dominate polarity in this pool.

rules.rationale: Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758); ring density raises hydrophobic surface and lowers aqueous solubility.
Source long-SMILES effect was strongly negative on solubility (-11.46); sign flip predicts higher lipophilicity.
Short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89) in source; small polar scaffolds should partition poorly into octanol.
Very long strings often encode polar or peptide-like scaffolds where added length does not add lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL ring and length effects with reversed sign, but is now downweighted relative to the domain-mechanistic model because the length relation had low confidence (0.22) and the sign flip is unverified. Fails if lipophilicity tracks polarity rather than size.

state.lesson: The halogen/aromatic domain model held its lead on development seeds, so the productive revision was reallocating weight toward the heteroatom polarity term rather than chasing the low-confidence sign-reversed length prior; source-transfer rules survive only as a downweighted hedge.
state.revision_summary: Kept the deployed halogen/aromatic partition model but strengthened the polar-heteroatom penalty and added a halogen-aromatic interaction while trimming the very-long-length counter to a two-condition design; reduced the sign-flip transfer skill to three rules with lower confidence, lower semantic mass, and a heavier UCB anchor, since its development AUC (86.36) trailed the domain model (88.70).
